sources.title: AI That Works: Product Specs with AI
AI That Works: Software Factory for Agent Tools
sources.note: Full transcript + README. Mostly Vaibhav/Dylan demo of BAML's loop; Dex contributes questions and framing.

sources.title: AI That Works: Agent Observability
sources.note: Full transcript + README. Vaibhav leads; Dex adds history, PR walkthrough, ARE skill, tech design doc.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: at each stage you have less clarity and more leverage
cards.claim: Design is a staged funnel (design 25k ft, outline 10k ft, then code) and each stage trades clarity for leverage, so decisions belong in the earliest stage.
cards.evidence_detail: Whiteboard framing, no numbers.
cards.landing: Ship plan §0 phase routine: design/outline gates before implementation
cards.inventory_ref: AI That Works #62 Product Specs with AI (2026-06 line)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: we actually dropped the plan step and we just started using a smarter model during implementation
cards.claim: HumanLayer dropped the separate plan step of RPI and relies on a smarter model during implementation for flexibility.
cards.evidence_detail: Stated as a product change, no measurement.
cards.landing: Phase routine: whether a separate plan artifact is needed; effort routing

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: you skipped the part of aligning on what is the actual like program gonna look
cards.claim: Splitting design into product design and technical design plus a program-design step (test seams, signatures, file layout) is needed because a design discussion can declare itself done while the implementation still comes out wrong.
cards.evidence_detail: Friction experienced in HumanLayer's own design discussions.
cards.landing: Ship plan phase routine: a program-design step before coding; a skill

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: models don't know that
cards.claim: Models default to patterns the codebase deliberately avoids (React providers/useEffect) so an up-front question like provider vs TanStack collection heads off the bad choice before the PR exists.
cards.evidence_detail: Repeated experience of rejecting phase-1 implementations; no counts.
cards.landing: Phase routine: explicit pattern-choice questions at outline time; CLAUDE.md invariants

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: how do you make it so that when the PR lands, it's already ninety nine percent correct
cards.claim: The goal of the upstream pipeline is a PR that lands 95-99% correct so review is easy, as an alternative to AI-review-only or no-review.
cards.evidence_detail: Stated goal; he says merging without review is not something he favours.
cards.landing: Opus reviewer per PR; owner view; gate placement

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: The further you are in the pipeline... the more tokens of surface that you're reasoning through
cards.claim: Later discovery of a wrong decision costs more tokens of surface for the model to reason through, so move verification and decisions earlier.
cards.evidence_detail: Reasoned argument; Dex notes the session is at 70K tokens, under 200K.
cards.landing: Phase routine ordering; one phase per session

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: we're only at seventy K tokens
cards.claim: Dex tracks context size explicitly and wants to finish design and outline sessions under the 200K-token range.
cards.evidence_detail: Number is a live reading of the demo session (70K tokens).
cards.landing: Context budget rule in phase routine (token ceiling per phase)

cards.author: other
cards.quote: The earlier you are, do more breadth. The later you are, do more verification.
cards.claim: Prompts should favour breadth early in a pipeline and verification late; Vaibhav's synthesis of Dex's process, which Dex endorses ('that's great').
cards.evidence_detail: Takeaway stated by Vaibhav; Dex agrees.
cards.landing: Prompt design for phase steps and refuters

cards.author: other
cards.quote: tell me what's different about the plan than what I implemented
cards.claim: A standardized 'what deviated from the plan' section in every PR makes the human verification loop faster than reading code; Dex confirms HumanLayer's PR step does this.
cards.evidence_detail: Vaibhav says it is the PR section he reviews every time and where he finds bugs.
cards.landing: Draft-PR body / six-question closing message (deviation-from-plan field)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: ask them during building to work with you on how we can measure success
cards.claim: Have the agent define a measurable success metric during product design so a later agent can check the numbers and decide whether the feature solved the problem; skip it for purely exploratory changes.
cards.evidence_detail: Technique described; skipped in the demo itself.
cards.landing: Phase routine: success/verification metric in plan; measurement pipeline (previously skipped)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: we're basically building the prompt for the next model, the next session
cards.claim: Markdown research docs are prompts for the next context window so they should be token-dense, while HTML is only for human-facing artifacts.
cards.evidence_detail: Design choice; Vaibhav adds he rarely feeds HTML to models, converting to SVG/PNG.
cards.landing: Evidence folders / handoff docs format rule

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: an intermediate representation that is like human readable and model friendly
cards.claim: Have the model write a human-readable intermediate representation (e.g. JSON AST) and compile it deterministically to the final artifact; qualified as truer a year ago.
cards.evidence_detail: SQL-via-AST example, he concedes models are now good at SQL.
cards.landing: Workflow scripts producing structured evidence

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: let the model benchmark its own work
cards.claim: For performance-sensitive work, have the model benchmark its own output rather than trusting one-shot generation.
cards.evidence_detail: One-line aside, refers to the performance-testing episode.
cards.landing: Verifier scripts / backpressure

cards.author: other
cards.quote: I actually stopped having Claude D in our repo. Because like stuff just gets out of date.
cards.claim: Vaibhav has no CLAUDE.md because a universal one skews the program more incorrectly than correctly; he uses conditional architecture.md files the model reads when relevant. Dex does not adopt this but engages seriously.
cards.evidence_detail: Team practice at BoundaryML, no measurement.
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md trim: move conditional content to on-demand docs

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: this important if syntax. This seems really useful in terms of giving the model permission to ignore
cards.claim: HumanLayer's CLAUDE.md is mostly a monorepo name map plus test/migration/log how-tos, and uses an 'important if' wrapper that tells the model when an instruction applies; he calls it a poor man's skills system.
cards.evidence_detail: Dex shows the file on screen; no length or adherence figures given.
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md trim/restructure: conditional sections, move how-tos to skills

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: context shards
cards.claim: A practitioner's 'context shards' pattern: 60-70 small snippets, the research/design phase selects the relevant ones, and the implementation session loads only 5-10 per phase.
cards.evidence_detail: Secondhand from a grocery-delivery engineer; Dex says HumanLayer is looking at it.
cards.landing: Knowledge-store design; per-phase context loading list

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: if your Claude touches files in a directory, it loads that directory's ClaudeMD
cards.claim: Directory-scoped CLAUDE.md and glob-scoped rules (Cursor/Claude rules) are the existing mechanisms for conditional context, though under-adopted.
cards.evidence_detail: Stated feature description; Dex says he knows no one using Claude rules.
cards.landing: Nested CLAUDE.md in backend/, technician-app/, src/ to cut root file

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: I will use shitty software that has a CLI over good software that doesn't.
cards.claim: Prefer tools with a CLI/MCP so agents can script them; agent-first, human-second design.
cards.evidence_detail: Personal preference stated at the opening.
cards.landing: Tooling choices for agent-accessible verification (CLIs over GUIs)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: it's all just loops
cards.claim: A software factory decomposes into loops that turn signal (vision, PM decisions, production errors) into agent work and give agents a way to check their own work.
cards.evidence_detail: Framing in the intro, attributed to recent social-media distillation.
cards.landing: Workflow library: named loops as reusable scripts
cards.inventory_ref: AI That Works #63 (2026-06 line) and 2026-06-26 video 'Building Your Own Software Factory'

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: you don't have to build the entire software factory at once
cards.claim: Build small isolated loops (e.g. a redraft-and-back loop), find leverage points for humans versus agents, and layer them rather than designing the whole factory.
cards.evidence_detail: Dex's closing takeaway.
cards.landing: Incremental workflow library; start by saving the loops already authored

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: a very human-friendly state machine for tracking the state of work
cards.claim: A tracker (Linear) is used as a human-friendly state machine for work; the sparse-human tracker holds links and text while artifacts live elsewhere.
cards.evidence_detail: Dex's characterisation; Vaibhav adds history analysis of redrafts to improve first drafts.
cards.landing: Decisions journal / register states; status labels as machine-readable phase state

cards.author: other
cards.quote: if checks are still failing after four or five agents were spawned
cards.claim: Both loops carry a max-turn cap (about 4-5 agent respawns) after which the item moves to a 'needs human' state and pings Slack; Dex sketches this as 'max turns'.
cards.evidence_detail: BAML team's practice; Dex adopts it in his diagram.
cards.landing: Workflow scripts: turn caps and escalation state

cards.author: other
cards.quote: let GitHub figure it out. Let our CI CD
cards.claim: Agents open the PR immediately and CI plus a review bot drive follow-up fix agents, rather than the agent running the full test suite in its own sandbox; test wait fell from 15-20 minutes to 2-4.
cards.evidence_detail: 15-20 min to 2-4 min test time; sequence of fresh agents per failure stage.
cards.landing: CI as the verifier in phase routine; fresh agent per failure round

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: hey, look, we did three rounds of editing and three rounds of PR checks
cards.claim: Apply a little human effort at the draft stage to avoid several rounds of edits, checks and review on a wrong approach; Dex ties it to last week's leverage point.
cards.evidence_detail: Reasoned comment.
cards.landing: Human gate on diagnosis before implementation (knowledge-store verified diagnoses)

cards.author: other
cards.quote: the best skill is actually not a long skill
cards.claim: An 'arena' runs the same task against several skill versions (branches) and measures cost, turns and success; the shortest skill won because a runtime describe command did the heavy lifting. Dex asks about metric and endorses reading friction from traces.
cards.evidence_detail: Reported outcome in BAML's arena; no numbers shown.
cards.landing: Skill A/B testing; trim CLAUDE.md/skill length by measurement

cards.author: other
cards.quote: every issue comes with evidence
cards.claim: Findings are deduplicated across runs and each carries the specific transcripts as evidence; later rediscovery of a deprecated issue appends new evidence; a pruning agent retests stale issues.
cards.evidence_detail: BAML team practice shown in the demo; Dex asks and accepts the design.
cards.landing: Knowledge store: evidence-attached diagnoses with dedupe and staleness pruning

cards.author: other
cards.quote: We are not yet confident enough in agents to be able to auto-merge
cards.claim: The loop ends at a human merge button; agent-drafted PRs need a human to approve or fix, with distinct ready-to-merge and needs-human labels. Dex asks to clarify the two states.
cards.evidence_detail: Team practice.
cards.landing: One-page owner view: separate 'ready' from 'broken'

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: anything that you can't trust the LLM to get right 99% of the time
cards.claim: Align at the technical-design-doc level on anything the LLM cannot be trusted to get right 99% of the time; 5-10 minutes there saves hours at code review and avoids code that looks fine but hurts maintainability within about four weeks.
cards.evidence_detail: Dex's ten years in large codebases; no measurement.
cards.landing: Phase routine: tech design doc trigger rule
cards.inventory_ref: AI That Works #64 Agent Observability (2026-07 line)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: even with system architecture defined and aligned... you can still end up with really bad code
cards.claim: Mermaid/sequence diagrams are not enough: even with aligned architecture models produce overlapping objects and bad interfaces, so review type signatures and object shapes before code.
cards.evidence_detail: Stated as common experience ('a lot of people are finding').
cards.landing: Outline step: signatures and objects, not just diagrams

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: a skill called application reliability engineering
cards.claim: HumanLayer's reliability skill makes the parent agent use only sub-agents (same model, 'RLM mode') to fetch logs, Sentry and traces so parent context stays sparse, then reads only summaries and writes an incident report.
cards.evidence_detail: Describes HumanLayer's live practice; no numbers.
cards.landing: Skill + workflow: sub-agent fetch, parent reads summaries only

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: just tell me what happened. Don't don't tell me what's wrong
cards.claim: To stop the model jumping to false conclusions, ask it to report what happened and list candidate causes, expecting the last several to be filler.
cards.evidence_detail: Dex notes Claude gets excited and states false conclusions.
cards.landing: Refuter/diagnosis prompts: separate observation from cause

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: an HTML file per folder that explains the changes in that folder at a high level
cards.claim: A review pattern he cites: the agent generates a per-folder HTML summary so 2000 changed lines can be digested in a minute with drill-down on demand; he links it to productising code understanding.
cards.evidence_detail: Secondhand from something he saw the prior week; HumanLayer also added a PR walkthrough feature.
cards.landing: Owner view / reviewer output format

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: show me the call stack
cards.claim: Trace during planning: ask the agent to show the call stack, type signatures and object relations before approving a plan, then feed the execution trace back and ask what the design missed.
cards.evidence_detail: Dylan's workflow described by Vaibhav; Dex presents it as part of planning.
cards.landing: Call-graph tooling (skipped by harness review) and plan review step

cards.author: other
cards.quote: Observability is useful in hindsight.
cards.claim: Instrumentation must exist before a bug occurs because it only pays off after the fact; trace everything by default, redact risky fields, and make traces queryable and typed so an agent can query them.
cards.evidence_detail: Vaibhav's thesis; Dex adds the history and agrees; includes OTel JSON-string blow-up claim (100 bytes to ~800) as an estimate.
cards.landing: Telemetry for routine compliance (was the store consulted); measurement pipeline (previously skipped); hooks

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Look at your damn data, as Hamel Hussein would say.
cards.claim: Inspect the actual traces and data rather than trusting summaries or vibes; Dex also ties this to doing vibe evals.
cards.evidence_detail: Aside at the close; attributes the phrase to Hamel Husain.
cards.landing: Evidence folders with sha256 manifests; review of real transcripts

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: 2026 is gonna be the year of no more slop
cards.claim: Industry reaction to slop at the conference ranged from more review agents and linting to new languages; Dex names no-slop as 2026's focus and notes 70% of attendees are early in their AI journey.
cards.evidence_detail: Conference impressions, 70/30 split is secondhand and anecdotal.
cards.landing: none specific; context for review/verifier priority

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: you can't YOLO it
cards.claim: If the agent's work cannot be seen (via design visualizations, traces or per-folder summaries) you cannot trust it; understanding must be cheap enough to maintain without reading every line.
cards.evidence_detail: Brief closing statement.
cards.landing: Owner view and reviewer artifacts

gaps: Transcripts are auto-captions with speaker labels; attribution by content was needed for several Vaibhav-led demos in the factory and observability episodes.

Inventory lists these episodes only in month-level one-line entries (and the 06-26 Building Your Own Software Factory video is a separate listing, probably this recording); exact section headings were not copied, so inventory_ref uses line descriptions.
No measured benchmark numbers from Dex in these three episodes; measured items (test time 15-20 to 2-4 min) are the BAML team's, not Dex's.
